Requirement: Each semantic-artefact release MUST identify its publisher, authority record and exact namespace/type scope. Verifier authorisation is specified separately by GOV-7.
Basis: CIR (EU) 2025/1569 Art. 8 (catalogue); SD-JWT VC Type Metadata publishers; WP

Requirement: Before acceptance, the verifier MUST establish issuer authorisation for the credential type and selected rulebook version using the authenticated authorisation snapshot selected by the recorded decision-time policy.
Basis: WP check 4; SD-JWT VC; HAIP §3.4 (out of scope there)

Requirement: An ecosystem claiming L4 publisher assurance MUST define an authenticated trust anchor and a supervised register schema that binds publisher identity, authority scope, keys, status and effective times.
In the reviewed-release module, each semantic release MUST have recorded approval of its exact source/release digest by two distinct authorised reviewers before release signing.
Semantic artefacts SHOULD identify the legal text and version they model, using an official identifier and effective date where available.
Conformance testing and access to the normative specification MUST NOT require enrolment with a designated private platform operator.

Before accepting a semantic release, the verifier MUST validate its publisher authorisation against the selected authenticated root: all delegation signatures and thresholds, namespace/type constraints, role separation, validity intervals, root version and revocation state must satisfy the profile's authorisation predicate.
Basis: TUF delegations; X.509 name constraints; formal model T17

Requirement: A release claiming the reproducible-build profile MUST provide verifiable provenance identifying reviewed source, complete pinned build inputs and deterministic build parameters, together with an independent rebuild producing the release digest.

Every release MUST publish a compatibility assessment containing L2 and L3 semantic diffs against the preceding release over a declared versioned corpus; detected or otherwise known incompatible changes MUST use a new immutable version identifier.
Basis: ROBOT/Bubastis diff; EBSI and eProcurement versioning rules

Requirement: The publisher MUST publish an authenticated canonical dependency manifest covering the complete supported context-resolution closure and every L3 dependency, including shape severity/openness and parent versions.
Basis: PoS L1(c); SHACL security (Chiem Dao & Debruyne)

Requirement: For each claimed pair of representation formats, the publisher MUST supply a versioned transformation specification and conformance vectors showing equal canonical RDF or equal defined application outputs, whichever equivalence the profile claims.

The publisher MUST declare an admitted input language, maximum sizes and deterministic work-budget semantics, and publish conformance vectors covering its admitted production boundary and adversarial cases.
Verifiers claiming this JSON-LD authoring-format module MUST accept only the authenticated built representation as a runtime semantic input, rather than processing YAML-LD source during verification.

In the machine-generated-source module, each release containing machine-generated semantic source MUST carry provenance identifying that source and an authorised human approval of its semantic changes before signing.
Basis: AI Act Art. 50 covers specific content categories only; this is the profile's own control

Requirement: Each published crosswalk MUST identify pinned source and target vocabulary versions and carry an authenticated versioned mapping specification with declared relation semantics, loss conditions and conformance vectors.

A verifier using a compiled context MUST authenticate its compiler/profile version and source-closure digest and verify the profile-required evidence that its processing semantics match that source closure.

Every closure offered for blank-node-free admission MUST carry a signed certificate binding its complete source/compiled closure digest, admitted document grammar, processor semantics/options, certificate-checker version and the sound admission property established by the named certification procedure.
Basis: Review finding R2-14; formal model T9.2

Requirement: Publisher release keys MUST be generated and used within an approved key-protection boundary whose certified or attested configuration prohibits plaintext key export.

In the policy-gated-signing module, the signing service MUST refuse release signatures unless it has authenticated all gate evidence required by a pinned policy and bound that evidence to the exact release digest and signing request.

In the independent-build threshold module, release signing MUST require the declared threshold of independently administered builders to contribute shares bound to the identical release digest after verifying their own reproducible-build results.
Each role's authenticated key-lifecycle policy MUST specify rotation, revocation effective time, compromised-key recovery, trust-anchor transition and the treatment of previously signed artefacts.

Every signing and verification role MUST enforce a versioned authenticated algorithm policy that specifies allowed algorithms/key sizes, effective dates, verification horizons and downgrade rules, including state-management rules for any stateful hash-based scheme.

Random seeds used for keys, nonces, salts or randomised assignments MUST satisfy the named entropy/RBG profile, with the profile-required source, health-test and generation evidence; deterministic derivations MUST use the separately specified approved construction. The same applies to whichever actor generates a hiding-commitment salt, including holders, and the salt MUST be encoded as fixed-length octets; this row is mandatory wherever M31 commitments are claimed.
Profile: Opt: entropy profile (mandatory with M31 commitments)

Requirement: A verifier MUST load each semantic dependency from bytes matching the authenticated closure manifest selected for the recorded decision context.

A verifier MUST refuse definitive acceptance unless every indispensable object in its authenticated metadata/status chain has valid signatures and hash/version links and is unexpired under the profile's trusted-time rule.

Before each use, the verifier MUST enforce the scoped rollback predicate: metadata is at least its durable high-water mark; the artefact version is at least its durable high-water mark unless explicitly authorised by a valid scoped downgrade; and the artefact is absent from its permanent withdrawal set.

A verifier requiring witnessed transparency MUST accept a release only with an inclusion proof under a checkpoint consistent with its retained checkpoint and cosigned under the profile's common, stateful, honestly intersecting witness-quorum policy.
Basis: RFC 9943 (architecture); witness cosigning with intersecting quorums (T7)

Requirement: The publisher MUST publish each release's status through an authenticated state machine in which withdrawal is a terminal, threshold-authorised event identifying the exact affected version and scope.
A verifier MUST enforce a profile-declared maximum clock error ε throughout each freshness decision and refuse definitive acceptance when it cannot establish that bound.

An offline verifier MUST cease definitive acceptance at the earlier of the declared offline deadline and expiry of any indispensable supporting evidence, and label further outcomes unknown or subject to a separate authorisation policy.

An archive operator supporting a long-lived carrier MUST retain and make retrievable by digest all manifest-specified decoding and interpretation inputs through the carrier profile's declared retention end date.
Basis: ESPR data carriers; Battery Regulation (passport from 18 Feb 2027)

Requirement: A compressed-carrier verifier MUST use the profile-specified authenticated binding to the complete decoding manifest in DST-12 and MUST consume only the output authenticated by the selected profile: signed-envelope deterministic decoding for B, or verified inner RDF graph for I-RDFC.

Under the declared network-observer model, the distribution protocol MUST make observable retrieval/update traces independent of the processed credential, except for explicitly declared leakage; conformance MUST test the specified trace-equivalence property.

A distribution profile MUST specify the authenticated object that asserts current status, its maximum lifetime Δ_status, its honest-signing/compromise assumptions, the checked metadata chain and the resulting cessation bound Δ_status + ε; outer timestamps MUST NOT refresh the validity of expired or stale underlying status evidence.
Basis: TUF timestamp/snapshot/targets expiries; review finding R2-04

Requirement: A compressed-carrier manifest MUST bind every decoding input that can affect output: registry and decoder/processing-model identifiers and versions, codec implementations or normative semantics, type and URL codecs, tables, transitive contexts, base/processing options and canonicalisation/normalisation rules.
Basis: CBOR-LD 1.0 WD (registry entries, codecs); review finding R2-13

Requirement: A transparency deployment claiming conflict detection MUST specify and operate an honest monitor that eventually retrieves all leaves through accepted checkpoints and checks a declared conflict relation over publisher, namespace, identifier, version, epoch and status.

In the authenticate-first module, the verifier MUST validate an approved lexical/envelope authentication gate binding the exact input before invoking JSON-LD expansion or RDF canonicalisation. A standalone RDF proof requires an independently specified bounded-processing profile or an additional gate; it does not conform to this module by itself.
Basis: PoS §5.4 (cheap pre-checks; residual: forged proof naming an allowed issuer); Fujie & Suzuki

Requirement: For the RDF module, the securing mechanism MUST bind the accepted RDF dataset to the issuer-authenticated canonical dataset or its signed commitment, with the processing profile identified. Closure archival and L3 interpretation MUST separately satisfy the closure requirements.
The verification cell MUST have no network capability and MUST accept external dependencies only through the authenticated, integrity-checked snapshot interface.
Basis: DI 1.0 §5.14 (network requests not required; defensive fetching allowed) — this is a stronger rule; Fujie & Suzuki (SSRF)

Requirement: A verifier claiming the blank-node-free RDF profile MUST reject inputs outside its normative admission grammar and MUST use a closure certificate tied to the complete closure digest, processor/options and grammar version, whose certification establishes that every admitted input expands without blank nodes.
Basis: PoS A1; F5 (lists with repeated values); review finding R2-14

Requirement: A verifier MUST derive any definitive budget-exceeded rejection from the profile's deterministic metering semantics; a wall-clock or resource interruption MUST yield unknown/retryable, not a cryptographic-invalid verdict.
Basis: PoS §9.1 (time limit with interrupt); rdf-canonize, rdf-canon limits

Requirement: When an authenticated representation is transformed into the application view, the verifier MUST reject loss of an authenticated, interpretation-relevant member except for omissions explicitly permitted by the selected transformation profile.

Issuers/publishers MUST authenticate a critical-extension declaration using the profile's scoped identifiers. Verifiers MUST reject unsupported critical extensions and MUST apply supported ones according to that profile; a closed-world profile MUST reject every unsupported extension.

A derived presentation MUST preserve the issuer-authenticated interpretation of each disclosed statement under the selected disclosure profile; the verifier MUST separately enforce the policy's required inputs and proofs. Selective disclosure of policy-irrelevant fields remains permissible once the complete required evidentiary basis is established; for compliance decisions, DEC-8 applies.

Before applying a status entry, the verifier MUST validate its pinned status profile and authenticated evidence against the profile's maximum age and trusted-time rules; unavailable or stale status MUST yield unknown.
Basis: Bitstring Status List; W3C #218; revocation series

Requirement: Raw-context caches MUST verify their content-addressed bytes. Processed-context caches MUST additionally key entries by all processing inputs, including effective/base URL, active context where relevant, processor/profile/options and trust domain.
Basis: jsonld.js #502, #537, PR #552 (functional bug, no security framing)

Requirement: Applications MUST consume the immutable authenticated view or the output of a pinned, approved derivation from that view.

Render metadata MUST NOT alter machine validation semantics unless explicitly admitted as a semantic dependency by the profile. Human-decision interfaces MUST identify and integrity-check any template on which the presented interpretation relies.
Verifiers MUST derive L3 interpretation solely from the pinned vocabulary/rule closure and the identified interpretation engine/configuration, including built-in mappings and inference rules.
Basis: PoS L1 (contexts only); formal model T2 (LFSC binds L2, not L3)

Requirement: JSON inputs MUST satisfy the declared I-JSON/JCS profile on raw UTF-8 text, including unique names, permitted Unicode, finite binary64 parsing and specified rounding; exact decimal quantities outside that model MUST use a specified string/typed-value representation. The authenticated parsed value MUST be passed immutably onward.
Basis: RFC 7493; RFC 8785 (assumes I-JSON); formal model T16

Requirement: Before accepting a credential proof, the verifier MUST establish from authenticated, current local authorisation evidence that the exact verification method is authorised by the credential's authenticated issuer for the required purpose and scope.
Basis: VC Data Integrity 1.0 (verification method and controller)

Requirement: Before semantic acceptance, the verifier MUST verify that every dependency actually used by expansion/interpretation is present in the authenticated closure manifest, including nested/scoped/imported contexts, relevant loader metadata, processor options and interpretation configuration; undeclared resolution MUST fail closed.
Basis: JSON-LD 1.1 embedded and scoped contexts; review finding R2-02

Requirement: Every replayable receipt MUST cryptographically bind the outcome and a manifest identifying the reconstructible decision context, including executable/configuration semantics and decision-relevant state, by authenticated digests. A replayable action receipt MUST also bind its profile and key epoch, request or challenge, subject, action and scope, audience and purpose, and role-labelled dependencies in one injective encoding; honest approval MUST be keyed to these exact bytes, and single-use actions MUST enforce consumption or equivalent idempotency.

A time-scoped decision MUST bind the selected historical/current closures, selection rule and authenticated time evidence. If certification time selects meaning, use the validated TSA generation time or trusted bounded log-inclusion time bound to the evidence digest; issuer-asserted event time alone MUST NOT select it.
Basis: Bi-VAKs, Temporal RDF (data, not decisions); HS 2028 (1 Jan 2028)

Requirement: Retained evidence SHOULD support the selected format's standalone proof re-verification. A long-term preservation profile MUST specify evidence renewal, algorithm migration and validation-material retention before relevant trust expires.
Basis: PoS Def. 5.1 (requirement); LFSC-G is a new means

Requirement: In the agent-authority module, admission tokens MUST bind the action, closure and authority epoch; accepting an applicable withdrawal MUST advance the epoch durably.

When required meaning or its verification evidence is unavailable, stale or indeterminate, the verifier MUST return unknown and MUST NOT authorise the action through that verification path; any escalation MUST use a separately authorised, recorded policy.
Basis: Revocation series ("stale is unknown"); AI Act Art. 14

Requirement: For the declared replay-retention period, the receipt custodian MUST preserve and retrieve by authenticated digest every dependency required to reconstruct the claimed decision, including executable semantics/configuration and relevant state; privacy/access restrictions MUST be part of the preservation profile.

An agent commit MUST atomically validate the token's action/closure authorisation against the current durable epoch and freshness/withdrawal state at the external effect's defined linearisation point. Where an effect depends on a co-signed receipt, it MUST NOT occur before that receipt is valid and these checks pass at that point; a provisional decision MUST NOT authorise the effect.

For a decision under an authenticated compliance-evidence profile, the verifier MUST accept an evidentiary basis only when the profile's required input sufficiency, coverage (DEC-9) and computation guarantees are established: verified complete sufficient key claims, a valid certificate (DEC-10, DEC-11), or disclosed claims or proofs whose sufficiency for the exact policy, closure and required decision guarantee is established. Holder choice over policy-relevant evidence MUST NOT determine the outcome.
Basis: T19; VER-8; PoS P2; customs H1/H7 data sets (Rukanova et al. 2026); WCO Data Model

Requirement: The governing compliance-evidence profile MUST identify the subject, action and purpose; the authoritative evidence domains and sources; identifier resolution and query or push coverage; the snapshot or cut-off; source authority and status; and the positive or absence evidence sufficient for every policy-relevant dependency. These choices MUST be authenticated independently of the holder, and missing, stale or inconsistent coverage MUST yield unknown.
Basis: T19.5; WCO Data Model; customs data requirements; audit completeness assertion

Requirement: A certificate issuer MUST validate the profile-required authenticated evidence and coverage, recompute the hiding commitment, evaluate the pinned policy, and sign a canonical core binding the outcome, privacy-preserving input, coverage and context bindings, closure and policy digests, scope, authorisation reference and retention manifest. Indeterminate required coverage MUST yield unknown. Trusted time MUST be external evidence over the signed core.

A relying party MUST check the certificate's proof, the issuer's authorisation for the decision class, an authorising outcome, the selected certificate, its subject, action, purpose, audience and time scope against the request, the applicable closure and policy, and the required certificate, issuer and dependency status. Missing or stale required evidence MUST yield unknown; effect authorisation MUST satisfy the applicable commit-point rule (DEC-7).
Basis: X.509 path validation and certificate policies (RFC 5280)

Requirement: A certificate lifecycle profile MUST index certificates by every decision-relevant dependency (policy, closure, inputs, status) and define invalidation, suspension, replacement and historical-replay rules. After an invalidating event, including a policy-only correction with an unchanged closure, current reliance MUST cease within the declared freshness bound until re-evaluation with current inputs succeeds; replacement MUST preserve and link the prior record.

Before treating a certificate as replayable, the verifier MUST validate a custodian acknowledgement of a verified deposit of the complete archive manifest, opening and recovery material bound to the certificate core. The custodian MUST demonstrate reconstruction on deposit and at profile-defined intervals, under defined continuity, access, retention and release rules.
Basis: RFC 4998; provable data possession; proofs of retrievability

Requirement: A dispute report MUST report separately the authenticity of the certificate and evidence, the validity of the opening, the reconstructibility of the context and the equality of the outcome. Missing evidence, inconsistent openings and computation mismatch MUST be distinct results, and any attribution of fault or statement of substantive correctness MUST name the additional evidence it relies on.

A profile claiming one authoritative evidence snapshot per scope and epoch MUST define an authenticated selection and supersession rule and enforce or detect conflicting selections through its consistency mechanism; verifiers MUST bind reliance to the selected snapshot.
Profile: Core (if a single authoritative snapshot is claimed)

Requirement: An implementation selecting the semantic-inventory module MUST produce a signed inventory of loaded closure/configuration digests. Operators SHOULD run a declared differential corpus against those versions and record divergences.
Basis: CycloneDX data components (static); EBSI conformance header

Requirement: An implementation claiming execution-bound attested decisions MUST enforce an isolated decision runtime and exclusive authorisation of its certified receipt key, bind receipts to the exact executed context and relying-party challenge, and enforce current engine authorisation across upgrade/restart. Replay-validated receipts are a separate claim governed by MON-6 and MON-7.
Basis: Linux IMA CRITICAL_DATA (SELinux policy); RATS, EAT

Requirement: Publishers MUST issue authenticated advisories under the designated advisory/withdrawal role with affected immutable identifiers, action, scope and publication time. Verifiers MUST process them according to the pinned advisory policy and freshness rules.

Agent deployments SHOULD compare the admitted closure digest with the closure used for each action and reject or re-admit on mismatch; semantic-change diagnosis requires a separate differential analysis.

The attested-engine module MUST specify and enforce authenticated engine/key-policy updates, version rollback protection, revocation, state recovery and register/index lifecycle, with relying-party appraisal tied to the same policy version.

A replay co-signer MUST authorise only the exact canonical receipt message whose committed input and context it has authenticated, found admissible under the independently anchored request policy (authorised closure, current authority epoch and status, declared clock tolerance), and evaluated to the proposed definitive outcome; an unresolved dependency or an unknown outcome MUST NOT authorise a share.
Basis: Hyperledger Fabric endorsement; CoSi witness cosigning

Requirement: A replay-signing profile MUST identify the threshold scheme, its security and corruption game, the authenticated group key, participant authorisation and key epoch, and MUST enforce the scheme's key-generation, nonce and session, restart, share-protection, rotation and revocation conditions; adaptive or mobile corruption claims require their own proof.

Before current reliance on an execution-bound or replay-validated receipt, the verifier MUST reject it unless an authenticated enrolment record from a governance-recognised authority satisfies the M24 acceptance predicate for the exact receipt key or group configuration, key epoch, claimed participant or device, approved engine and key-policy versions, responsible legal person and authorised scope at the defined use or commit point.
Basis: RATS (RFC 9334); IEEE 802.1AR; TCG TPM 2.0 device-identity keys; RFC 8995; eIDAS Art. 35 (seals); agent–owner credentials [draft-ni-wimse-ai-agent-identity]; NIST NCCoE agent-identity concept paper (2026); harness WE-3 E3; review record (S5)
Ev: — (proposed; WE-3 E3 demonstrates only the key-certification limit)

Requirement: The profile specification SHALL define format-neutral security objectives and a requirements-applicability matrix for each supported format, with equivalent evidence and test obligations where mechanisms differ.
Each conformance module MUST publish positive and negative vectors for every applicable attack class, identify unsupported/untested classes, and define the expected outcome and applicable role.
Basis: OpenID HAIP conformance; Fujie & Suzuki vectors

Requirement: A conformance claim MUST identify the profile version, applicable format/modules, role, requirements satisfied and evidence for any declared assurance level.
A technical conformance claim MUST NOT assert legal recognition or cross-jurisdiction equivalence unless separately established under the identified legal framework.

The authenticate-first module MUST specify maximum input/field sizes and an auditable preauthentication operation/memory budget; under the stated cost model, total preauthentication work MUST be O(n log n) or better plus the declared bounded number of cryptographic operations.
A verifier MAY cache results only after binding the request to the exact authenticated input and all decision-relevant dependencies; cache reuse MUST satisfy PRF-5.

The issuer MUST verify that the complete encoded carrier payload, including signatures, bindings, version/algorithm identifiers and error-correction overhead, fits the declared carrier/profile capacity.
Agent deployments SHOULD declare hardware, workload/adversary envelope, latency percentile and overload behaviour, and measure the selected verification profile against that budget.

A cached result MUST be reused only while its authenticated input, processing/configuration, issuer-key authorisation, trust/policy/status snapshots and time-dependent predicates remain valid; negative or unknown entries MUST have bounded lifetime/storage and MUST NOT suppress re-evaluation after a relevant dependency changes.
Basis: PoS caching (T2, L3); review finding R2-15

Requirement: A profile claiming availability MUST specify its admitted input/workload and resource envelope, dependency-reachability assumptions and retention horizon, and demonstrate the declared bound to a definitive result under those conditions, with explicit overload/partition outcomes. Where decisions depend on replay co-signing, the envelope MUST include a reachable, willing qualified quorum (n − f ≥ t), coordinator and progress assumptions, terminating deterministic evaluation and permitted context access, and its tests MUST distinguish safe refusal or deferral from completion.

A profile claiming presentation unlinkability MUST use presentation-specific identifiers supported by its authenticated disclosure/re-randomisation scheme and MUST demonstrate that exposed identifiers/proofs do not enable linking under its stated observer model.
Basis: `ecdsa-sd-2023` HMAC relabelling (identifiers stable per credential); review finding R2-03

Requirement: A status-index privacy module MUST define its assignment distribution, adversary knowledge, audit relation and permitted leakage, and provide a specified proof/audit procedure that verifies assignment policy without revealing protected mappings.

A masking profile MUST identify an immutable version of its cover-entry lifecycle rules and conformance vectors; its documentation MUST state the residual correlation/leakage and MUST NOT claim privacy from cover entries alone.

Shared evidence deployments SHOULD minimise exposed identifiers and commitments under a declared observer/data-protection model, use access-controlled indirection and appropriately hiding commitments where needed, and apply retention/access/deletion policy to pointers as well as payloads.

A resolution-privacy profile MUST declare the observer/permitted leakage and ensure credential-dependent identifiers, cache misses, message sizes, timing, failures and retries do not influence exposed resolution traffic beyond that leakage.
Basis: Oblivious HTTP (RFC 9458); OCSP stapling; review finding R2-20

Requirement: An evidence-certification profile claiming confidentiality MUST specify the permitted leakage of the entire public certificate, presentation, status and locator transcript, and MUST bind private inputs in public digests only through hiding bindings; personal-data processing MUST define purpose-specific necessary inputs, recipient and custodian access, and retention. Any unlinkability claim MUST use a supported presentation scheme and an observer-model test.
Basis: GDPR Art. 5(1)(c); review findings R2-27 and R3-12
